title.en: Know the format of a ledger account
Post journal entries and balance accounts

say.en: The journal lists transactions by date, so cash entries are scattered over many pages. The ledger collects them in one account to answer such questions quickly. In this lesson: Know the format of a ledger account.
Post journal entries and balance accounts.

body.en: The *ledger* is the principal book of accounts. It contains all the accounts of the business, each on a separate page, in the form of a T: Date, Particulars, Journal Folio (J.F.) and Amount on both the debit and credit sides. Accounts may be classified as asset, liability, capital, revenue and expense accounts.
body.kn: ಖಾತೆ ಪುಸ್ತಕ ಪ್ರಧಾನ ಲೆಕ್ಕ ಪುಸ್ತಕ. ಅದರಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರತಿ ಖಾತೆಗೆ ಪ್ರತ್ಯೇಕ ಪುಟ, ಡೆಬಿಟ್ ಮತ್ತು ಕ್ರೆಡಿಟ್ ಬದಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ದಿನಾಂಕ, ವಿವರ, ಜೆ.ಎಫ್. ಮತ್ತು ಮೊತ್ತ.

body.en: To post a journal entry, go to the account debited and write on its debit side "To" followed by the name of the account credited; then go to the account credited and write on its credit side "By" followed by the name of the account debited. To balance an account, total both sides, write the difference on the smaller side as "Balance c/d", and bring it down on the opposite side as "Balance b/d".
body.kn: ಡೆಬಿಟ್ ಆದ ಖಾತೆಯಲ್ಲಿ "To" ಎಂದು ಕ್ರೆಡಿಟ್ ಖಾತೆಯ ಹೆಸರು, ಕ್ರೆಡಿಟ್ ಆದ ಖಾತೆಯಲ್ಲಿ "By" ಎಂದು ಡೆಬಿಟ್ ಖಾತೆಯ ಹೆಸರು ಬರೆಯುವುದೇ ವರ್ಗಾವಣೆ. ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸವನ್ನು c/d ಮತ್ತು b/d ಆಗಿ ತೋರಿಸಿ ಖಾತೆ ಮುಚ್ಚಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

problem.en: Post the cash entries of Kavya Traders to the Cash Account and balance it: Apr 1 capital ₹1,50,000 received; Apr 3 deposited into bank ₹60,000; Apr 8 cash sales ₹25,000; Apr 12 salary paid ₹8,000.

steps.en: Debit side: Apr 1 To Capital A/c 1,50,000; Apr 8 To Sales A/c 25,000; total 1,75,000.
Credit side: Apr 3 By Bank A/c 60,000; Apr 12 By Salary A/c 8,000; total so far 68,000.
Balance = 1,75,000 − 68,000 = 1,07,000, written as Apr 30 By Balance c/d 1,07,000; both sides now total 1,75,000.
May 1: To Balance b/d 1,07,000 on the debit side.

narration.en: Let us work this out step by step. Post the cash entries of Kavya Traders to the Cash Account and balance it: Apr 1 capital ₹1,50,000 received; Apr 3 deposited into bank ₹60,000; Apr 8 cash sales ₹25,000; Apr 12 salary paid ₹8,000.

say.en: Let us work this out step by step. Post the cash entries of Kavya Traders to the Cash Account and balance it: Apr 1 capital 1,50,000 rupees received; Apr 3 deposited into bank 60,000 rupees; Apr 8 cash sales 25,000 rupees; Apr 12 salary paid 8,000 rupees.
Debit side: Apr 1 To Capital A over c 1,50,000; Apr 8 To Sales A over c 25,000; total 1,75,000.
Credit side: Apr 3 By Bank A over c 60,000; Apr 12 By Salary A over c 8,000; total so far 68,000.
Balance equals 1,75,000 minus 68,000 equals 1,07,000, written as Apr 30 By Balance c over d 1,07,000; both sides now total 1,75,000.
May 1: To Balance b over d 1,07,000 on the debit side.
So the answer is Cash A over c debit balance 1,07,000 rupees.
